text: Ten fictional nonprofit passages, each with eight quote variants for testing a citation checker.

passages.source_passage: During the third quarter of 2023, the Kalembe Camp case management team registered 412 new protection cases, a rise of 18% on the previous quarter. Caseworkers completed initial assessments for most households within five working days. Unaccompanied children accounted for sixty-three of the new cases, and each was referred to the interim care unit run by Haven Bridge Relief. Follow-up visits did not reach the eastern blocks in August because flooding closed the access road for nine days. Monitoring staff noted that female caseworkers handled the majority of gender-based violence disclosures. The team has not yet resolved the backlog of 74 files awaiting closure, and supervisors recommend recruiting two additional caseworkers before the dry season.

variants.paraphrase: Unaccompanied minors made up 63 of the new cases, and all of them were sent to the interim care unit operated by Haven Bridge Relief.

passages.source_passage: The mid-term evaluation of the Tamarind Skills Centre in Oruvale found that 286 young people enrolled between March 2022 and June 2023, against a target of 300. Completion rates were strong, with 81% of enrolled trainees finishing their six-month courses. Welding and solar installation attracted the highest demand, while tailoring places often went unfilled. Employers in the district praised the practical assessments, but the centre has not formalised placement agreements with any of them. Graduates who secured work earned an average of 1,450 shillings per week. The evaluators did not find evidence that the mentoring component improved job retention, largely because mentors met trainees fewer than four times. They recommend that the centre restructure mentoring before the second phase begins.

passages.source_passage: Board members will be pleased to hear that the Ndovu Care Circle home-visiting programme reached 1,120 clients across Lisanda and Mbewe wards in the first half of 2024. Volunteers made an average of three visits per client each month, delivering adherence support and basic wound care. Viral load suppression among clients with recent test results rose to 87%, up from 79% a year earlier. However, the programme did not receive its expected shipment of home care kits in April, and volunteers improvised with locally purchased supplies. Twelve volunteers left during the period, mostly citing travel costs. No client deaths were linked to missed visits. Management is asking the board to approve a modest transport stipend of 200 kwacha per volunteer per month.

passages.source_passage: Kiboro District has some of the lowest sanitation coverage in the Upper Nalu region. A baseline survey conducted by Clearspring Water Trust in 2022 found that only 34% of households had access to an improved latrine, and fewer than half of the district's 58 primary schools had a functioning water point. Most villages rely on two hand-dug wells that dry up between July and October. Women and girls walk an average of 4.5 kilometres each day to collect water. Previous boreholes drilled in the area were not maintained because no water committees were trained to manage repairs. The proposed project will drill 12 new boreholes, construct latrines in twenty schools, and establish a committee at every water point.

passages.source_passage: In 2023 the Harvest Thread Savings Initiative supported 146 village savings and loan groups across Mabinda and Torreo counties, up from 112 the year before. Members, of whom 78% were women, saved a combined 9.6 million francs and issued more than 3,400 small loans. Most loans financed petty trade, livestock and school fees. The share-out at the end of the cycle returned an average of 21% on members' savings. Not every group performed well: eleven groups in Torreo dissolved after disputes over loan repayment. Field officers did not visit those groups as often as planned because two motorcycles were out of service for most of the year. We have since replaced both motorcycles and introduced a quarterly dispute-resolution training for group leaders.

passages.source_passage: The Little Lanterns playgroup network now operates 37 community playgroups in the Fenwick Valley, serving roughly 640 children aged two to five. Since the last board meeting, facilitators have completed a refresher course on play-based numeracy, and attendance has averaged 82% across the network. Parents in Hollin Cross asked facilitators for an afternoon session, which began in September. Not all sites are thriving. Four playgroups in the upper valley have not met regularly since heavy rains damaged the shared hall. We were unable to secure a replacement venue, and the parish council has not responded to our request. Staff will present options for relocating these groups at the November meeting, including a mobile toy library that visits each village twice a month.

passages.source_passage: The Rukanda District Health Partnership now supports 214 community health workers across nine sub-counties. Between January and June 2024, they conducted 18,600 household visits and referred 1,230 children with danger signs to health facilities. Malaria testing at community level rose by 26%, largely because rapid diagnostic tests were in steady supply for the first time in two years. Stipends were not paid on time in March, and several workers in Kibowe sub-county paused activities for a week. The district health office has not yet confirmed whether it will absorb stipend costs after 2025. Supervisors report that community health workers trust the new mobile reporting tool, although older workers asked for more training. Management recommends the board fund a second training round in August.

passages.source_passage: The Sundarpur Mothers' Outreach Project held 96 outreach clinics in Barhan and Kesra blocks during the quarter, an increase from 71 in the previous quarter. Midwives registered 1,048 pregnant women, and 64% of them attended at least four antenatal visits. Institutional deliveries among registered women reached 812, while home births fell sharply. However, postnatal follow-up within 48 hours remains weak, and many newborns were not checked by a health worker in their first week. The project did not open the planned second clinic in Kesra because the landlord withdrew from the lease in July. Volunteers continue to accompany women to the district hospital, and the ambulance partnership with Sevaan Transport has reduced average travel times to under an hour.

passages.source_passage: The Grainbridge School Meals Programme served hot lunches in 52 primary schools across the Dossa and Kanté districts during the 2023–24 school year. On average, 14,300 pupils received a meal on each school day, and head teachers reported that attendance rose by 11% compared with the year before the programme began. Local farmer cooperatives supplied 40% of the millet and beans. Deliveries did not arrive on schedule in February, and nine schools went without meals for up to six days. Cooks are mostly unpaid mothers, and several schools have not been able to retain them. Management asks the board to approve a small honorarium for cooks and to fund storage upgrades so that schools can hold a two-week reserve of grain.

passages.source_passage: The Puente Claro Scholarship Fund currently supports 318 girls in lower and upper secondary schools across the departments of San Ildefonso and Valle Moreno. This term, 92% of scholars maintained the required attendance, and 41 girls in their final year sat national exams in November. Mentors met with each scholar at least once a month, and parents attended two community meetings on safe transport. Not every scholar stayed enrolled: seven girls left school, most of them because of early marriage or family migration. The fund did not raise its uniform and book allowance this year, although costs rose by about 15%. Staff recommend that the board approve a modest increase so that families are not forced to choose which daughter continues studying.
